findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "fetch" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "wrangle" stacks urgency/override words (never, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch, describe, rows, wrangle, sql_query, upload_request, upload_confirm · Private data: fetch, describe, rows, wrangle, sql_query, export, upload_request, upload_confirm · Public sink: rows, upload_request, upload_confirm · Destructive: wrangle, sql_query, export.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch, describe, rows, wrangle, sql_query, upload_request, upload_confirm · Private data: fetch, describe, rows, wrangle, sql_query, export, upload_request, upload_confirm · Public sink: rows, upload_request, upload_confirm · Destructive: wrangle, sql_query, export

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
